newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Indian blue chips up,premiums pressured.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Indian blue chips up,premiums pressured.

text.p: Global Depositary Receipts recovered slightly from a sharp drop at the start of the week, with some fresh bidding among blue chips, traders said.
"Some like Hindalco and SBI were bid up," said one trader. "But there was also profit-taking in high premium GDRs like Bajaj."

Bombay's benchmark 30-share index was up 51.71 points or 1.56 percent to a provisional 3,375.93 close, but off the day's high of 3,379.33. Hindalco was at 23.25, up 0.57 on the day and State Bank of India (SBI), which bore the brunt of trader disappointment at the end of last week, was at 18.25, from around 17.75 yesterday.
Traders said there were still only a "nebulous" message from the Indian government on economic reforms but a more pressing concern was the impact on the economy of higher oil prices.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 1.15 point or 1.80 percent up at 65.37, with the premium over the local market at 12.68 percent compared with yesterday's 12.11 percent.

The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up just 0.12 percent with a premium of 46.54 percent over the local market, with the index at 67.76. The Taiwan GDR Index finished down 1.52 or 1.47 percent at 101.39, with a premium of 4.68 percent.
